summary: Step 7 Pros & Cons Wizard — three fixes verified. Issue #1 (Auto-ladder Std Rating chips) PASS. Issue #2 (Realistic Gap selector) PASS. Issue #3 (Persistence on Next→Back) PARTIAL — factor-level Expected/Unit persist correctly, but cell-level Actual + Assess% race condition still loses Actual when both unmount-flush PUTs fire in parallel. Also fixed a CRITICAL bundle-blocking import bug (useRef missing from React import) that made Step 7 throw ReferenceError and render nothing.

critical.issue: Read-modify-write race condition. When two parallel PUTs hit the same cell (e.g. one for actual_value and one for assessment_pct, fired simultaneously from DebouncedInput unmount-flush on Next), the second handler reads stale doc, applies its partial patch on top of the stale cell, and _persist() overwrites the first handler's write. Net effect: only the last PUT's fields survive — the other field is reset to its prior value. Repro: clear cell → fill Actual=55000 + Assess%=75 → click Next within 100ms → backend ends up with assessment_pct=75 but actual_value=''. Fix options: (a) MongoDB atomic $set on nested keys assessments.{oid}.{fid}.{field} in _persist, OR (b) frontend coalesces all pending cell-level saves for the same (oid,fid) into a single merged PUT body during unmount/flush.

ui_bugs.issue: useRef was used (lines 116-119) but missing from React import — entire Step 7 crashed with ReferenceError: useRef is not defined, blocking ALL rendering on Step 7. Fixed during testing by adding useRef to the import list on line 1.

integration_issues.issue: Cell Actual value not persisted when typed alongside Assess % then Next clicked before debounce (race with concurrent PUTs — see backend critical bug). rca_of_issue: Race condition: DebouncedInput.flush() is called per-input on unmount. With 2 inputs on the same backend cell (Actual + Assess%), 2 parallel PUTs hit upsert_assessment. Both handlers call _load_analysis (reads doc snapshot), mutate their field on the cell, then _persist({assessments: assessments}) which overwrites the WHOLE assessments dict. The later writer wins, losing the earlier writer's field. Sequential typing (with debounce gap >600ms between fields) does NOT exhibit this — backend test confirmed actual_value='55000' + assessment_pct=75 both survive when saves serialize. Reproduced reliably on 2 consecutive runs with the same outcome (assessment_pct=75 wins, actual_value='' loses).
